it without reading the DB by hand. For every ACTIVE Solana watch it lists
the automations bound to it and compares each automation's `triggerSpec`

event), flagging the mismatches that drop an event silently: a stale chain
(`solana-mainnet` on the spec while the watch/event is devnet), a specific
topic0 that is not the any-event wildcard, a program-id/chainFamily
mismatch, or an inactive automation.

it. `stale` means it ran but stopped > 3m ago. Otherwise read `lastError`
first (connection/auth), then each chain's `connected` + `subscribedPrograms`.

get.summary:
Redis memory headroom — poll this from an uptime monitor.

A full Redis makes BullMQ reject every write (lock renewal, job completion,
dequeuing), which silently halts sending and loses in-flight jobs. Returns
`level: ok | warning | critical | unknown`; alert on anything but `ok`.
Samples live rather than serving a cached reading so a probe always sees
current state, falling back to the last scheduled sample on error.

Primary readiness probe. Checks DB, cache, and worker heartbeats for
configured groups when Redis is enabled.

Only components listed in `HEALTH_REQUIRED_COMPONENTS` (default:

adds `degraded: string[]` naming the down-but-tolerated components.

redirects, so a click never lands the recipient on an error page.

info.title: Onchain Suite
info.description:
The OnChain Suite backend API.

## Response envelope

**Every successful (2xx) response is wrapped**, and the schema shown for each
endpoint below describes the value under `data` — not the whole body. A global
interceptor wraps it as:

```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Request processed successfully",
  "data": <the documented payload>,   // the schema shown on the endpoint
  "meta": { "totalItems": 0, "page": 1 },  // present only on paginated lists
  "timestamp": "2026-10-22T10:30:00.000Z",
  "requestId": "…"
}
```

So read a documented `ConnectorDirectoryEntryDto[]` as `data: ConnectorDirectoryEntryDto[]`.
Server-sent-event streams (`text/event-stream`) are the only exception — they
are not wrapped.

## Error envelope

**Every error (4xx/5xx) has one shape**, produced centrally, regardless of which
endpoint threw it:

```jsonc
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "CONNECTION_SECRET_REQUIRED",  // stable — branch on THIS
    "message": "A credential body is required…",
    "details": { }                          // optional structured context
  },
  "meta": { "timestamp": "…", "path": "/api/v1/…", "requestId": "…" }
}
```

Branch on `error.code` (stable `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`), never on the HTTP
status (shared by many failures) or the English `error.message` (reworded
without notice). Common codes: `BAD_REQUEST`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`,
`NOT_FOUND`, `DUPLICATE_ENTRY` (409), `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMITED`
(429), `INTERNAL_ERROR`, plus domain codes a handler sets.

## Auth

Most endpoints need a session (bearer / session cookie). Org-scoped endpoints
read the active organization from the request and additionally enforce a role
(`OWNER`/`ADMIN`/`EDITOR`); a missing session is `401`, an insufficient role
or wrong org is `403`.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code — branch on this. A domain code when the handler threw one, else the status spelled (BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, …).

message.example: A credential body is required, e.g. { "botToken": "..." } for Telegram.
message.description: Human-readable message — for logs/display, not for branching.

details.description: Optional structured context (the thrown payload, field names, …).

scope.description:

text.description: Prometheus exposition-format payload from the queue worker.

confirm.description: Must exactly equal the queue name in the URL. Guards against a mistyped or copy-pasted request hitting the wrong queue.

mode.description: 'clean' removes jobs in the given states and leaves queue structures intact (default). 'obliterate' destroys ALL queue data including active jobs — irreversible.

states.description: States to clean. Defaults to ['wait','delayed'] — the parked backlog — deliberately NOT 'active', which would orphan jobs mid-send.

limit.description: Maximum jobs to remove per state in one call.

grace.description: Only remove jobs older than this many milliseconds. 0 means all ages.

filename.description: Original filename (used only to infer an extension when `ext` is absent).

contentType.description: Intended content type (advisory; the upload PUT sets the real header).

ext.description: Explicit extension for the stored blob (e.g. `csv`, `json`, `ndjson`).

blobPath.description:

format.description: Override the inferred format. Otherwise derived from the blob extension.

contentType.description: Content type recorded on the synthesized file (defaults to `text/csv`).

onConflict.description: Conflict resolution when a match already exists.

dedupeKey.description:

email when present, else wallet — so a mixed CSV keeps every row that has
at least one identity.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for interpreting date columns.

maxErrors.description: Abort the job after this many row errors.

zk.description: Force ZK protection on imported contacts.

expireInHours.description:
Grace period, in hours, before the OUTGOING key stops working.

Defaults to `0` — immediate. That is the right default because the usual
reason to roll is a leak, and a default grace period would leave a
compromised credential live. Pass 24–72 for a planned rotation, so servers
can be redeployed without downtime. Capped at 168 (7 days).
